segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Lucy, we really need to get working on this marketing assignment. We've only got five weeks left to the end of term to design it, carry it out, and then write up the results.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: Sure. Well, let's get started right now. Let's go over the instructions. What exactly do we have to do?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Well, it says here we have to look at one area of the entertainment industry. There's a list of the different types.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: What are they?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Music, cinema, theatre, sport, and eating out.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: Is that all?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Looks like it.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: So we choose one branch of the industry and then we look at how two different groups of people use it? Is· that right?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yes.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: And do we have to use any particular method to get our data? Can we mail out a questionnaire, or do face-to-face interviews, or maybe even observations?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Well actually, it looks like we don't have a choice. We have to do telephone interviews.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: OK, so at least we don't have to waste time deciding between the different methods.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yeah, that's right. Oh, and the other requirement is the number of interviewees.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: ·Not too many, I hope. Ten? Twenty?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Well, we have to do two groups, remember, and it looks like we have to interview fifteen for each group.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: That's thirty altogether then. It's going to take ages.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yes, but remember we're working on this together, so we'll only have to do fifteen each.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: OK, so those are all the requirements?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Yes, looks like it.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: So, first, which area are we going to choose? My preference would be cinema, since that's where I spend most of my money.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Hmm, I don't think that's such a good idea. I don't think there are huge differences ip the market there. I mean you get young and old, male and female, rich and poor all going to the same movtes.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: Yeah, maybe you're right. Let's make it music then.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Right. So, what two groups will we compare and contrast?

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: Male and female?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: No. Most of my female friends like the same music as me. Different age groups would be much more likely to show up differences, I think.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: Yeah, I suppose you're right again. I'll take some notes, shall I? So .. . Age Groups. Well. What do you think? Maybe twenty-five or under for one group, and forty-five or over for the other group? That should show up differences.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: OK. Next. How about the kind of music they like -let's give them some choices and then we can just tick boxes.

segments.speaker: IACK
segments.en: OK. Let's have pop, jazz, folk, easy listening ... What else?

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: Well, we should include classical. Some people like it, you know.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: OK. OK. And then we should have how they listen to music.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: The medium. Right. Let's include radio, CD- and then I guess there's

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: What about concerts? You know, in pubs and halls.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: Oh yeah, we should include live music of course.

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: OK, we're on a roll now! Next point could be about where they actually get their music.

segments.speaker: LUC Y
segments.en: You mean like, do they buy it in music shops, or department ~?

segments.speaker: JAC K
segments.en: Yes, or download it from the Internet.

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: Right. That could be for recorded music. Then we need another section for live music. Where do they go for that?

segments.speaker: JACK
segments.en: OK. Let's say disco, pub, llil.Q, concert hall . . .

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: Or opera house! And I guess we should include karaoke bars.

segments.speaker: JAC K
segments.en: Not many of them in this city!

segments.speaker: LUCY
segments.en: OK. We'll leave that out then. So, what's left to do?

segments.speaker: JAC K
segments.en: That's it. Well, now we can make a time-scale for doing it.
